title: The Beast of White Orchard
text:
The Beast of White Orchard is the first main quest of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt after the prologue at Kaer Morhen. Geralt and Vesemir stop in the village of White Orchard, where a griffin has been attacking travelers.

The investigation uses Witcher Senses to follow blood trails and claw marks, includes questioning the hunter Mislav, and leads to the site where a dead griffin — the attacker's slain mate — is examined with Vesemir. Preparing for the fight involves brewing or buying bait and choosing signs and oils effective against beasts.

The quest ends with the griffin fight outside the village. Completing it leads into events at the tavern and the journey to Vizima.

title: Lilac and Gooseberries
text:
Lilac and Gooseberries is an early main quest of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt. Geralt searches the region of Velen for the sorceress Yennefer, whose trademark scent of lilac and gooseberries identifies her trail.

The quest is a tracking investigation: questioning peasants and Nilfgaardian soldiers, examining campsites and belongings with Witcher Senses, and following leads toward the sorceress' destination. It also opens the way into the larger Velen storyline around Crow's Perch and the Bloody Baron.

Following Yennefer's trail eventually points Geralt toward Skellige as the next step of the search.

title: Vesemir
text:
Vesemir is the oldest living witcher and the venerable sword-combat instructor of the School of the Wolf at the keep of Kaer Morhen. He is Geralt's mentor and something of a gruff adoptive father figure to the witchers of his school.

In The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt he appears in the prologue at Kaer Morhen while Ciri trains, then travels with Geralt at the start of the search for her. He is cautious, experienced, and often the voice of restraint compared to younger witchers.

title: White Orchard
text:
White Orchard is the first open-world region of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt: a small farming village in Temeria under Nilfgaardian occupation after the war. It serves as the tutorial area where the player learns exploration, Witcher Senses, combat, alchemy, and Gwent.

Notable places in and around the village include the notice board, the tavern, the sawmill, the Nilfgaardian garrison camp, the local smith, and the fields and mill where the griffin attacks travelers.

title: Witcher Senses
text:
Witcher Senses are the core investigation mechanic of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, activated by holding a button. While active, the world is tinted and important traces stand out: blood, footprints, sounds, scents, and objects of interest glow red.

Quests frequently require following these tracks to locate monsters, people, or clues, and to examine highlights in the environment. Witcher Senses also let Geralt eavesdrop through walls and spot items that are otherwise easy to miss.
